Subject: HealthForge — follow-up & items from today's discovery

Hi Emma — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can get security/compliance aligned before the pilot: 

- Scope & intent: HealthForge wants to embed a guided triage assistant for clinician-facing workflows. Data will include patient metadata (hashed IDs), clinical notes snippets, and configuration metadata.
- Key asks from your side: confirmation of data jurisdictions, SOC 2 status, any HIPAA requirements tied to the pilot, and the list of cloud partners/subprocessors that will touch patient data.

Can you please:
1) Share a high-level subprocessor roster (cloud infra, logging, analytics, monitoring) — a simple spreadsheet is fine.
2) Confirm whether you require a full SOC 2 Type II report or a SOC 2 summary/attestation.
3) Indicate if PHI will be stored at rest or only transiently processed.

I looped in Aditya (sales engineer) to help with the architecture questions and Marissa (security) for the compliance thread if/when you want to route evidence.

Suggested next step: 30-minute compliance sync with your security owner + our security lead. Proposed slots: Thu 9/23 10:00–10:30 PT or Fri 9/24 11:00–11:30 PT. Let me know what works.

Thanks — Stephanie

--

Thanks Stephanie — good call. Quick answers inline: 

- Subprocessors: I pulled together a P0 roster (see below). I'll export a sheet for you by EOD.
  * Cloud infra: AWS (us-east-1 primary), GCP (backup analytics), Azure (limited R&D workloads)
  * Logging/observability: Datadog (prod logs), Sentry (errors)
  * Analytics: Mixpanel (event-level analytics, non-PHI), BigQuery (aggregated analytics)
  * Monitoring: CloudWatch (infra), Prometheus (k8s)

- SOC 2: We have a SOC 2 Type II for core platforms; procurement prefers receiving SOC 2 attestation + a short summary of controls.

- PHI handling: For the pilot we plan to pseudonymize then store minimal context in a secure bucket (PHI is stored at rest in AWS S3 with server-side encryption). We can provide a brief data flow diagram.

We can do the compliance sync Fri 9/24 11:00 PT — security@healthforge.com (cc'd) will join. I'll send the spreadsheet and a diagram by EOD.

Best,
Emma

Thanks for the heads up. Recommended evidence package (minimal, prior to pilot):

1) SOC 2 Type II attestation (PDF) or SOC 2 summary + auditor contact if they cannot share the full report.
2) Subprocessor roster with roles and data access level (read-only, read/write, admin). Prefer spreadsheet with columns: provider, purpose, data types, region, contact.
3) Data flow diagram (high level) showing where PHI is stored and which subprocessors touch decrypted data.
4) Encryption details: SSE settings for S3, KMS key ownership, TLS in transit.
5) Data retention policy for the pilot and default KV cache TTLs; confirm whether any logs contain PHI and how they're redacted.

Also ask for:
- Identity/Access: do they use SSO (Okta) and will they require SCIM/Just-in-Time provisioning for RBAC?
- Contractual: any PoCs with explicit HIPAA language they insist on.

For our call, Aditya — prepare a 1-slide operational plan that maps Redwood artifacts to the items above (e.g., where we store KV cache, options to zero-retention, quantization to avoid persisting tokens). I'll join Fri 9/24 11:00 PT.

If they can't share SOC 2 immediately, we can accept an attestation + proposal to provide full report under NDA.

Marissa
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
